issue.title: Confirm the dev-update prebuild cache actually hits on a real ,U and report the before/after timings
issue.description:
Epic sase-i9 ('Make dev-install SASE updates fast') closed with its headline claim measured only in parts. Its plan (plans:202608/fast_dev_update.md, 'verify' phase, item 1) asked for a median cargo-seconds comparison of core-changed and core-unchanged runs before vs after, plus the prebuild hit rate. That comparison is still not possible: no real ',U' has run since the prebuild cache landed.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN (verified on the host 2026-08-09 while landing sase-i9):
  - The background producer works end to end. ~/.sase/cache/rust-prebuild/ holds a mirror clone checked out at an incoming upstream sase-core commit (443f1aa), two completed stamped sets (retention 2, so pruning works), and last-result.json recording {"hit": true, "set_key": "27b89954466b3b1fc3b90d17"}. That set's stamp.json carries all six provenance fields (core_commit, cargo_lock_sha256, rustc 1.97.1, profile dev-update, python_abi cpython-314-x86_64-linux-gnu, target_interpreter .../uv/tools/sase/bin/python3) plus sha256 digests for both artifacts, and the 13M sase_core_rs.abi3.so and 12M sase-xprompt-lsp are present.
  - The producer's and consumer's checkout resolution agree in production: the live runtime inventory reports the editable sase-core-rs record with source_root == git_root == /home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase-core, which is what the producer receives as --source-root and what _rust_prebuild_core_root passes as --core-root.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN:
  - _consume_prebuild has never installed a stamped set during a real update. ~/.sase/logs/dev_update.jsonl contains only two timed records, both schema 2 (2026-08-09T12:48:31-04:00, rust_dev_install 399.4s; 2026-08-09T14:44:41-04:00, rust_dev_install 157.8s), i.e. both from before the prebuild commit bumped the journal to schema 3. Neither carries a rust_prebuild field.
  - So 'tools/dev_update_timings' cannot yet show the epic's before/after or the hit rate, and nobody has seen the ',U completes in seconds' outcome the epic promised.

SCOPE (small): after the host has run at least one real ',U' that advances sase-core, read ~/.sase/logs/dev_update.jsonl for the schema-3 record, confirm rust_prebuild.hit is true (or record the exact miss reason), run 'tools/dev_update_timings', and post the numbers against the baselines already recorded on sase-i9.1 and sase-i9.2. If the record shows a miss, diagnose the reason field (stamp-missing / commit-mismatch / lockfile-mismatch / rustc-mismatch / profile-mismatch / abi-mismatch / interpreter-mismatch / digest-mismatch / copy-failure / health-check-failed / disabled) and fix the mismatch. This is a read-then-report check, not a rebuild; do not invoke the rust install recipes from an agent shell (see sase-in).
